convertibility_reason: Uses no indicators at all — logic is purely based on raw candle body analysis (comparing close vs open and body size across consecutive bars). Simple market orders with fixed SL/TP, no grid/martingale, no custom indicators, no external .mqh with custom logic. Trade.mqh is standard MT5 library.

derived_values.name: up_1
derived_values.formula: count of last N bars where close < open (bearish candles)

derived_values.name: dn_1
derived_values.formula: count of last N bars where close > open (bullish candles)

derived_values.name: up_2
derived_values.formula: count of bars [1..N-1] where |close[i]-open[i]| > |close[i-1]-open[i-1]| (increasing body size), incremented alongside dn_2

derived_values.name: dn_2
derived_values.formula: same as up_2 — both up_2 and dn_2 are incremented together whenever body size increases from bar i-1 to bar i

custom_logic_notes: Entry logic: BUY when all N consecutive bars are bearish (close<open) AND body sizes are increasing across those bars. SELL when all N consecutive bars are bullish (close>open) AND body sizes are increasing. The up_2/dn_2 counter is shared — both increment together for any increasing body size, regardless of candle direction. Signal close functions always return false — exits are purely SL/TP driven. Buy SL = Ask - N*Point, Buy TP = Ask + N*Point; Sell SL = Bid + N*Point, Sell TP = Bid - N*Point. StopsLevel validation is performed before order placement. Bars are copied from index 1 (last completed bar) going back N bars, so signal is computed on the most recent N closed bars.
python_conversion_notes: Very straightforward. No indicator handles needed. Convert the Indicators() function to count bearish/bullish candles and increasing body sizes from the last N closed bars. Entry: if all N bars bearish with increasing bodies → buy; if all N bars bullish with increasing bodies → sell. Fixed lot, fixed SL/TP in points. New-bar guard ensures one signal per bar. No close signals — pure SL/TP exit. The up_2/dn_2 variables are identical in behavior (both increment together), so a single 'increasing_bodies' counter suffices.
